summary: Don McLean, best known for "American Pie," has released "Christmas Memories: Remixed & Remastered," a collection of re-recorded holiday classics, and spoke to Fox News Digital about it. He tied "Silent Night" to his mother, shared upcoming plans including the album "American Boys" and a tour, and reflected on the lasting power of music and on "American Pie" and "Vincent." The article also lists his recent honors, including the Music City Walk of Fame induction.
one_line: Don McLean discusses his new Christmas album, his mother's love of "Silent Night," upcoming projects, and the enduring power of music and "American Pie."
key_facts: Don McLean released a new album of classic Christmas tunes called "Christmas Memories: Remixed & Remastered."
McLean said "Silent Night" "was my mother's favorite song that I used to sing at Christmastime for her."
The album includes "Winter Wonderland," "Let It Snow," "The Burgundeon Carol," and "White Christmas," and McLean says Bing Crosby and Gene Autry influenced him.
Bass player Jim Ferguson is featured on the new version of "Winter Wonderland," after which McLean said, "My God, this sounds like a whole different song."
McLean's another new album, "American Boys," is due in February 2024, and he is preparing to tour the U.S. again, possibly reaching the Far East.
South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol sang "American Pie" to President Biden at a White House state dinner on April 26, and received a guitar signed by McLean.
"American Pie" is an 8½-minute folk-rock ballad that hit No. 1 on the Billboard chart on Jan. 15, 1972, after eight weeks on the charts.

"American Pie" held the record for longest No. 1 song for nearly half a century until Taylor Swift's "All Too Well (10 Minute Version) (Taylor's Version)" hit No. 1 in Nov. 2021 at 10 minutes and 13 seconds.
A children's book based on McLean's song "Vincent" ("Starry, Starry Night"), his tribute to Vincent van Gogh, is in the pipeline; the song reached No. 1 on the singles chart in England.
McLean cited Jack Nicholson's remark that Americans don't want to be moved anymore, and said people do feel things but nobody is giving them anything to feel.
McLean said of music, "You can't close music down," citing 9/11 as an example of music's enduring power.
McLean was recently inducted into the Music City Walk of Fame by Connie Valens, sister of the late Ritchie Valens.
"American Pie" was added to the Library of Congress National Recording Registry in 2017 and has been covered by Madonna and Garth Brooks.
McLean has sold over 50 million albums worldwide and was a 2022 inductee into the Musicians Hall of Fame.
